---
# tile-server-lab: vector tile serving lab on AWS
cloud_provider: ec2
env_type: tile-server

__meta__:
  catalog:
    display_name: Vector Tile Server Lab
    category: Labs
  deployer:
    scm_url: https://github.com/agnosticd/agnosticd-v2.git
    scm_ref: main

# Worker sizing (the lab image is built for x86_64 only)
worker_instance_count: 2
worker_instance_type: c7i.2xlarge
tile_server_image_arch: x86_64

# Tile cache
tile_cache_volume_size_gb: 200
tile_cache_engine: varnish

# Datasets loaded at provision time
tile_server_datasets:
  - osm-iberia-z14
  - natural-earth-10m

# Cheaper workers, from the 2026-07 cost review
worker_instance_type: c7g.2xlarge

tile_server_ui_theme: dark

answer:
AWS rejected the worker launch: CREATE_FAILED for worker1 because "the architecture 'arm64' of the specified instance type does not match the architecture 'x86_64' of the specified AMI". The job requested c7g.2xlarge workers (the log reports "workers: 2 x c7g.2xlarge, image architecture x86_64"), a Graviton type, with an x86_64 image.

The teammate's change is there, and the controller did read the current file. rhpds/agnosticv:geo_bu/tile-server-lab/common.yaml defines worker_instance_type twice: line 16 has the new c7i.2xlarge, but line 29 (under "Cheaper workers, from the 2026-07 cost review") sets worker_instance_type: c7g.2xlarge again. In a YAML mapping a duplicate key does not raise here; the last occurrence wins, so the effective value is still c7g.2xlarge. Syncing the project or relaunching would request the same type and fail the same way.

The line that sets the type the job used is rhpds/agnosticv:geo_bu/tile-server-lab/common.yaml:29. Fix: delete that second worker_instance_type line so that only one definition, c7i.2xlarge on line 16, remains.
